key_insight: A GPT2-based table-to-text framework showed strong disease-prediction performance on small clinical datasets, including thyroid cancer recurrence—not cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support research into thyroid cancer recurrence prediction when labeled data are scarce, but clinical readiness is not established.
method: Convert structured clinical records into physician-style text.
Use GPT4-generated medical paraphrases to improve minority-class representation, then fine-tune GPT2.
Apply gradient-based explainability to identify influential clinical features.
evidence_signal: Across four public datasets, the abstract reports average precision of 0.96, specificity of 0.97, sensitivity of 0.96, and F1-score of 0.96, with improvements over comparator models.
watch_item: The abstract does not report external clinical validation or whether paraphrase generation was isolated to training data to prevent leakage.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
